direction: Use an $N$-homotopy: overshoot to 76–78 points, then prune back to 74. Starting from the incumbent, insert 2–4 extra points at largest-empty-cap locations, anneal the enlarged (harder) problem for 30–50s so neighbourhoods reorganise under pressure, then delete the points with the worst combined score (maximum cosine, contact degree at $10^{-7}$, and sum of top-5 cosines) to return to 74 and repolish; also run the reverse path (drop to 70, anneal, reinsert 4 points one at a time with polishing between insertions). idea: Hub-and-rattler surgery that deletes rattlers plus top hubs to reach 6/10/14 removals and greedily reinserts each hole with 20k samples plus tangent subgradient refinement before annealed LogSumExp and minimax rebalancing.
direction: Perform hub-and-rattler surgery instead of random kicks. From the incumbent, delete all 0-contact rattlers plus the 2–4 highest-contact hubs (degree $\ge9$ at threshold $10^{-7}$) and, in successive trials, delete 6, 10, or 14 points total; greedily reinsert each deleted point by sampling 20,000 random sphere candidates, scoring them by maximum cosine to the current set, locally refining the best 20 candidates by tangent subgradient descent on that score, and inserting the best. Freeze the surviving core for the first reinsertions, then unfreeze and run the usual annealed LogSumExp plus active-set minimax; this directly converts wasted rattler capacity into new points placed in the largest holes while removing the over-constrained hubs that lock the old graph.

idea: Build an isotropic fresh population with Riesz-Adam plus frame penalties and create chimeras by Procrustes alignment plus greedy max-cosine subset selection.
direction: Build a diverse fresh population with isotropy pressure and recombine it by Procrustes crossover, rather than always starting from the record. Generate 6–10 independent starts by minimising Riesz/Thomson-type energies with Adam plus explicit penalties $\|X^{T}X-(74/13)I\|_F^2$ and $\|\sum_i x_i\|^2$ (weight decaying to zero), polish each briefly with LogSumExp annealing, and keep starts that are mutually distant in Gram-spectrum/contact-graph distance; then for pairs of parents, rotationally align them by orthogonal Procrustes ($UV^{T}$ from the SVD of $X_a^{T}X_b$), merge the two 74-sets, greedily select 74 of the 148 points minimising the running maximum cosine, repair with largest-hole insertion if duplicates were dropped, and repolish. This searches for a more symmetric, balanced basin from scratch and creates chimeric contact topologies that neither parent possessed.

idea: Deterministic rattler-hub surgery with hole-scored transplants, frozen-then-free annealed LogSumExp L-BFGS and trust-region LP polish under degree-sequence archive.
direction: Implement deterministic rattler–hub surgery instead of random kicks: compute contacts at slack \(<10^{-7}\), list rattlers (degree 0) and hubs (degree \(\ge7\)), and generate short trials that relocate one hub, or a hub plus its highest-contact neighbour, into a rattler’s hole—specifically sample 20,000 unit candidates, score them by their maximum cosine to the non-moving 72 points, take the best candidate perturbed by \(0.05\)–\(0.20\) rad in a random tangent direction, and transplant the hub there. Freeze the transplanted point for the first \(\sim\)200 annealed LogSumExp Adam/L-BFGS steps at \(\tau=10^{-3}\), then unfreeze and polish at \(\tau=3\times10^{-4},8\times10^{-5}\) followed by a 1–2 s trust-region LP polish; enumerate rattler/hub choices in shuffled order under a strict 120 s trial budget, keep an archive keyed by sorted contact-degree sequence, and only spend the final polish on trials whose degree sequence differs from the incumbent or whose post-polish score is within \(10^{-6}\) of best.

idea: Archive of distinct basins from tangent kicks, N-homotopy and random starts with Procrustes-Hungarian crossover of low-energy halves and hub-to-rattler swaps plus hole repair and LSE/minimax polish.
direction: Build a small archive of genuinely distinct local minima and recombine them by Procrustes crossover rather than perturbing one incumbent: generate 8–12 parents from the record with Gaussian tangent kicks of sizes \(0.03,0.08,0.15,0.30\), from 70/78-point homotopy variants, and from one or two random starts, polishing each only coarsely to the \(0.209\)–\(0.215\) range with time-boxed Adam-LSE. Fingerprint parents by sorted pairwise cosines and contact-degree sequences, discard near-duplicates after orthogonal Procrustes alignment (Hungarian matching on \(X_aX_b^\top\), then SVD rotation), and for unlike parent pairs construct children by aligning them, copying the 37 points with lowest per-point maximum from one parent and the complementary matched points from the other, or by replacing all hub points of one parent with matched rattler/low-degree points of the other; normalise, repair any near-duplicate rows by largest-hole resampling, then fully LSE+LP polish only children whose fingerprints are new, keeping global-best checkpointing throughout.

Egalitarian two-level LogSumExp per-point minimax with annealed temperatures and adaptive point weights to balance contacts, alternated with trust-region LP squeeze.
direction: Change the objective to an egalitarian per-point minimax so the core is relieved and rattlers are recruited: replace the single global LogSumExp over all 2701 pairs by a two-level smoothing, first \(m_i(\tau)=\tau\log\sum_{j\ne i}\exp(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle/\tau)\) for each point, then minimise \(\tau_2\log\sum_i \exp(m_i/\tau_2)\) with \((\tau,\tau_2)\) annealed from \((2\times10^{-3},10^{-3})\) to \((5\times10^{-5},2\times10^{-5})\), optionally with multiplicative point weights updated every 50 steps by \(a_i\leftarrow a_i\exp(20(m_i-\max_k m_k))\) and renormalised. Alternate 3–5 cycles of this balanced phase with ordinary global-max LP polish, explicitly reporting the spread \(\max_i m_i-\min_i m_i\) and number of zero-contact points; accept intermediate states that reduce rattlers or equalise \(m_i\) even at equal global max, because those are the topology changes the usual objective cannot see, then finish from the most balanced state with the standard LP squeeze and return the best verified configuration before 170 s.

idea: Lift the 13D code to S^13 in R^14 with small random 14th coordinate, reorder contacts with 14D LogSumExp L-BFGS, then squeeze back by joint optimization over the 14x13 Stiefel basis and the points with a geometrically increased subspace penalty.
direction: Use a 14D lift-and-squeeze dimension homotopy to reach a different 13D topology: embed the incumbent in \(\mathbb R^{14}\) with a small random 14th coordinate (\(\sigma=0.01,0.03,\) or \(0.08\) over several seeds), optimise 74 points on \(S^{13}\subset\mathbb R^{14}\) where the extra freedom should lower the maximum and rearrange contacts, then gradually squeeze back by optimising over a \(14\times13\) orthonormal basis \(W\) (parametrised by a skew-symmetric matrix via matrix exponential or by repeated QR retraction) while alternating fixed-\(W\) LSE polishing of the 14D points and \(W\)-steps that minimise the projected 13D LogSumExp objective, with a penalty on the discarded coordinate increased geometrically until it is \(<10^{-10}\). Project, renormalise, and LP-polish in 13D, trying at least 4 random lifts in the time budget; this directly searches for a configuration whose natural contact graph is balanced in one higher dimension and survives projection, instead of endlessly re-polishing the hub-and-rattler graph already found.

idea: Rattler-to-hub pair-splitting with penalised equalisation and simulated-annealing acceptance to reach a new balanced basin.
direction: Perform rattler-to-hub pair-splitting with non-greedy acceptance, rather than moving rattlers to the deepest hole (which merely recreates rattlers). Identify the 8 rattlers (row-max below global max) and the highest-degree hubs; for each trial, relocate one rattler to $ \mathrm{normalize}(x_h + \varepsilon u)$, where $x_h$ is a hub and $u$ is a unit tangent vector at $x_h$ pointing away from the hub's tightest neighbours, with $\varepsilon$ chosen so the new point is initially just above the target cosine from the hub, deliberately splitting the hub's contact load. Optimise a penalised objective $F_\tau(\text{LSE}) + \lambda \sum_i (\text{rowmax}_i - \text{global max})^2$ with $\lambda$ annealed upward to force row-max equalisation, and accept intermediate worsenings up to $\sim10^{-4}$ under a cooling simulated-annealing schedule instead of rejecting them outright, before a final exact minimax squeeze.

idea: Deterministic rattler-hub surgery with largest-hole transplants, frozen-core annealing and LP polishing toward a balanced isostatic optimum.
direction: Implement deterministic rattler–hub surgery instead of random kicks: compute contacts at slack \(<10^{-7}\), list rattlers (degree 0) and hubs (degree \(\ge7\)), and generate short trials that relocate one hub, or a hub plus its highest-contact neighbour, into a rattler’s hole—specifically sample 20,000 unit candidates, score them by their maximum cosine to the non-moving 72 points, take the best candidate perturbed by \(0.05\)–\(0.20\) rad in a random tangent direction, and transplant the hub there. Freeze the transplanted point for the first \(\sim\)200 annealed LogSumExp Adam/L-BFGS steps at \(\tau=10^{-3}\), then unfreeze and polish at \(\tau=3\times10^{-4},8\times10^{-5}\) followed by a 1–2 s trust-region LP polish; enumerate rattler/hub choices in shuffled order under a strict 120 s trial budget, keep an archive keyed by sorted contact-degree sequence, and only spend the final polish on trials whose degree sequence differs from the incumbent or whose post-polish score is within \(10^{-6}\) of best.

idea: Large-neighbourhood delete-and-rebuild on connected contact subgraphs with fingerprint diversity gate and frozen-set hole reinsertion.
direction: Use large-neighbourhood delete-and-rebuild on connected contact subgraphs with a diversity gate. Repeatedly delete a connected set of 12–20 points (a hub, its contact neighbours, and any nearby rattlers), freeze the remaining 54–62 points, and rebuild the deleted points one at a time by largest-empty-cap insertion (20k random candidates plus local hole refinement against the frozen set) followed by a joint LSE polish in which only the rebuilt points move; unfreeze and fully polish only if the rebuilt code's fingerprint (sorted top-200 pair cosines and degree sequence at tolerance $10^{-4}$) is measurably different from every archived basin, otherwise discard it cheaply. Cycle through many such deletions with different seeds under strict per-iteration time checks, archive the best few distinct basins, and always retain the best feasible 74-point code found so far as the return value.

idea: Multi-point block transplants into well-separated largest empty caps plus broad random-basin sampling with annealed LogSumExp L-BFGS and greedy worst-pair splitting to escape the over-polished hub-plus-rattler basin.

Basin-hopping walker with temperature acceptance wandering from current (not only best) via kicks/hole-transplants and fast two-stage LogSumExp L-BFGS plus greedy worst-pair splitting, without slow LP.
De novo feasibility continuation from random spheres with batched Adam on hinge loss at infeasible targets 0.2075/0.2065/0.2055 followed by low-temperature LSE Adam polish and worst-pair splitting.
direction: Run a de novo feasibility continuation that never starts from the record. Fix target cosines $t = 0.2075, 0.2065, 0.2055$ in sequence and, from 20–30 random spherical starts, minimise the hinge loss $\sum_{i<j}\mathrm{relu}(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle - t)^2$ with Adam and per-step renormalisation (equivalently retraction), so only violating pairs generate gradient and intermediate configurations may cross the current minimax barrier; whenever the loss hits zero, record the code and lower $t$, otherwise carry the least-violating configuration to the next stage. Finish any feasible or near-feasible code with a short low-temperature LSE polish plus active-set minimax, enforce a hard internal deadline near 150s with the incumbent returned throughout, and keep only basins whose sorted top-200 Gram fingerprint differs from the record's.

idea: Search C37/C36 orbit codes with distinct rotation frequencies and L-BFGS on LogSumExp over ~24 generator parameters, then release symmetry for full polish with fallback to best.npy.
direction: Search symmetry-constrained orbit constructions, which enforce regularity and no rattlers by design. Use a cyclic group $C_{37}$ acting on $\mathbb{R}^{13}$ as rotations by $2\pi k m_j/37$ in six coordinate 2-planes plus one fixed axis, take two full orbits ($37+37=74$) generated by two unit vectors, and optimise only the $\sim$24 generator parameters (block radii/phases per generator) by L-BFGS on the LogSumExp of the full $74\times74$ Gram; scan random frequency sets $(m_1,\dots,m_6)$ with distinct values in $1..18$. Also try the $C_{36}$ template ($36+36$ plus 2 axial poles). Spend at most $\sim$120s on the symmetric search, then release the symmetry and full-polish the best orbit code, falling back to `best.npy` if it does not improve.

idea: Metropolis wandering basin-hopping with hole-optimal multi-point transplants, hub-offload and large kicks plus annealed LogSumExp L-BFGS and active-set squeeze to force topology changes.
